description: A Next.js App Router route handler sets wildcard CORS through a headers object ("Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*") — the usual way route handlers and edge functions set CORS, since there is no res.setHeader. It is the same wildcard VC009 reports for cors() and setHeader("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"), so VC009 should fire on the header line: this fixture records that form gap, at the same risk level as those forms. The route answers for the signed-in seller, but the wildcard alone does not let another site read that: browsers refuse to share a credentialed response under "*", and the Auth.js session cookie (SameSite=Lax) is not sent on a cross-site fetch. KNOWN GAP: VC009 matches only the call form setHeader("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*"), not the object-literal form. Matching it would also report the corsHeaders block of every Supabase Edge Function (Supabase's own template, present in several existing fixtures) — a noise/consistency decision for the product owner, not a contained rule fix.
